difference.question: How is SlimPDF different from iLovePDF or Smallpdf?
difference.answer: SlimPDF uses server-side Ghostscript, the same compression engine used by professional print shops. Browser-based tools use JavaScript which typically achieves 20-40% reduction. We achieve up to 90%.

security.question: Are my files secure?
security.answer: Yes. All transfers use 256-bit encryption. Files are automatically deleted after 1 hour (free) or 24 hours (Pro). We never store or analyze your content.

targetSize.question: Can I compress to a specific file size?
targetSize.answer: Yes! Pro users can set a target like 'under 10MB' for email. We iterate compression until we hit your target while maintaining readable quality.

watermarks.question: Do you add watermarks?
watermarks.answer: Never. Your files come out clean on all plans.

api.question: How does the API work?
api.answer: Pro subscribers get REST API access for all tools. Simple endpoints, code examples in Python, JavaScript, and curl. 100 requests per hour included.

signup.question: Do I need to sign up?
signup.answer: No signup required for free tier. Compress, merge, or convert up to 2 files per day without an account.

platforms.question: What platforms are supported?
platforms.answer: SlimPDF works in any modern browser on Mac, Windows, Linux, iPad, and mobile. No software to install.

batch.question: Can I process multiple files at once?
batch.answer: Pro users can batch process up to 20 files at once across all tools. Results download as a ZIP file.

seoContent.title: The Best Way to Compress PDF Files Online

content.heading: Why PDF Files Get So Large
content.text: PDF files grow large for several reasons: embedded high-resolution images, multiple fonts, form data, annotations, and metadata. A simple report can balloon to 50MB if it contains unoptimized images or scanned pages. SlimPDF's Ghostscript engine analyzes your PDF and compresses each element intelligently, reducing file size without destroying quality.

content.heading: Browser Compression vs Server Compression
content.text: Most free PDF compressors run JavaScript in your browser. They're limited by browser memory and can only apply basic compression, typically achieving 20-40% reduction. SlimPDF runs Ghostscript on dedicated servers, the same engine used by professional publishers. This allows compression ratios up to 90% and handles files that would crash browser-based tools.

content.heading: When to Use Each Compression Level
content.text: Maximum compression is best for text-heavy documents, forms, and files you need to email. Balanced compression works well for documents with some images where you want good quality and smaller size. Minimum compression is ideal when quality is critical, like portfolios, presentations with photos, or documents for printing.

content.heading: Compressing Scanned PDFs
content.text: Scanned documents are essentially large images wrapped in PDF format. These often compress dramatically, sometimes by 80-90%. If your scanned PDF is too large, SlimPDF can reduce it significantly while keeping text readable. For best results on scanned docs, use Maximum compression.

quality.question: Will compression reduce my PDF quality?
quality.answer: SlimPDF uses intelligent compression that removes unnecessary data while preserving visual quality. Text stays crisp, images stay clear. For documents where quality is critical, use Minimum compression to prioritize appearance over file size.

howMuch.question: How much smaller will my PDF get?
howMuch.answer: Results depend on your PDF content. Documents with many images typically compress 60-90%. Text-heavy PDFs may compress 20-50%. Scanned documents often see the best results. You'll see the exact reduction after compression.

email.question: How do I compress a PDF for email?
email.answer: Upload your PDF, select Maximum compression, and download the result. If you need a specific size (like under 10MB for Gmail), upgrade to Pro and use the Target Size feature to compress to exactly the size you need.

secure.question: Is my PDF secure?
secure.answer: Yes. All uploads use 256-bit SSL encryption. Files are processed in isolated containers and automatically deleted after 1 hour (free) or 24 hours (Pro). We never access, read, or store your content.

batch.question: Can I compress multiple PDFs at once?
batch.answer: Pro users can batch compress up to 20 PDFs simultaneously. Upload multiple files, compress them all with one click, and download results as a ZIP file.

api.question: Can I compress PDFs via API?
api.answer: Yes. Pro subscribers get full REST API access. Send a PDF via HTTP POST, receive a compressed version. See our API docs for code examples in Python, JavaScript, curl, and more.

encrypted.question: Can I compress a password-protected PDF?
encrypted.answer: You'll need to remove the password first. If you know the password, use our PDF Unlock tool to remove protection, then compress the unlocked file.

size.question: What's the maximum file size?
size.answer: Free tier accepts files up to 20MB. Pro tier handles files up to 100MB. For files larger than 100MB, contact us about our Business tier.

mobile.question: Can I compress PDFs on my phone?
mobile.answer: Yes. SlimPDF works in mobile browsers on iPhone and Android. No app required. Just open slimpdf.io, upload your PDF, and download the compressed version.

offline.question: Does this work offline?
offline.answer: No. SlimPDF requires an internet connection because compression runs on our servers. This is what allows us to achieve 90% compression ratios that browser-based tools can't match.
